reversals.claim: I've left the trio and now perform solo exclusively.
reversals.user_update_task: I've left the trio and now perform solo exclusively, so can you help me write a short bio for my gig listings?
reversals.own_notes_doc: Sep 6: Solo piano, Blue Lantern wine bar, two sets. Sep 13: Solo, hotel lobby, three hours. Sep 20: Solo recital at the community arts center. Oct 4: Solo, Blue Lantern again. Note: told the bassist and drummer in August that I'm leaving the trio, and they're continuing with a new pianist. All bookings from now on are solo only. Need to work up more stride and left-hand bass patterns to fill out the sound without a rhythm section, and build a longer list of solo arrangements.
reversals.own_notes_task: Here's my gig calendar for the autumn. Can you help me plan practice priorities around it?

reversals.claim: I've shifted from bebop to modal and free jazz.
reversals.user_update_task: I've shifted from bebop to modal and free jazz, so can you help me put together a listening list to dig deeper?
reversals.own_notes_doc: June 2: Put the bebop fake book on the shelf. Worked on modal vamps over a single Dorian chord for 20 minutes. June 5: Free improvisation session with a saxophonist friend, no chart and no form, about 40 minutes. June 9: Learning quartal voicings built in fourths. June 12: Recorded myself playing over a drone in D and listened back. Plan for July: two modal tunes per week and one open free session. Not practicing rhythm changes heads or bebop lines anymore.
reversals.own_notes_task: Can you read my June practice journal and turn the July plan into a weekly schedule?
reversals.probe: Which tunes should I learn next?

reversals.claim: I've switched from piano to upright bass as my main instrument.
reversals.user_update_task: I've switched from piano to upright bass as my main instrument, so can you help me find good exercises for intonation?
reversals.own_notes_doc: Bought a used 3/4 upright bass in March and have played it every day since. Piano is now a secondary instrument that I use for composing only. Taking weekly bass lessons on Thursdays. Working on walking lines, intonation in thumb position, and building calluses. Sold the stage piano to help pay for a pickup and an amp. Need to get the bass setup checked because the action is high, buy a gig bag with wheels, and find a spare set of strings before the next gig.
reversals.own_notes_task: Here are my notes about my instruments. Can you make a shopping and maintenance list from them?
reversals.probe: What instrument maintenance should I schedule this month?

reversals.claim: I've moved from live performance to studio session work.
reversals.user_update_task: I've moved from live performance to studio session work, so can you help me write a short pitch email to recording studios?
reversals.own_notes_doc: April: Three studio sessions, two for a singer-songwriter album and one for a TV ad jingle. No club gigs booked. May: Five sessions, mostly reading charts on the spot and overdubbing piano parts. Learned to work to a click and deliver clean takes quickly. June: Started building a home recording setup for remote sessions. Turned down two club gig offers, since live work is no longer my focus. Rate: 150 dollars per three-hour session. Need to update my website to list studio credits.
reversals.own_notes_task: Can you read my Q2 work log and help me estimate my income for the next quarter?
reversals.probe: What should I focus on improving to get more work this year?

reversals.claim: I've stopped morning scales and now practice only repertoire.
reversals.user_update_task: I've stopped morning scales and now practice only repertoire, so can you help me organize my tune list into weekly practice rotations?
reversals.own_notes_doc: New practice routine since last month. Mornings are now 60 minutes of repertoire only, with no scales or technical exercises. I pick three tunes from my list, play through the head, comp a chorus, and improvise two choruses on each. Technique gets worked out inside the tunes whenever a passage is hard. I feel more ready for gigs this way. Current list: fourteen tunes. I want to add two new ones per month and record one run-through each week to check progress.
reversals.own_notes_task: Here are my practice notes. Can you suggest which kinds of tunes I should add next?
